data.title: These little-known investments could be among the best bargains in a crash
data.description:
By Brett Arends

In these febrile markets, be prepared

As market turmoil spreads, be prepared - for opportunities

If this stock market turmoil turns into a full-blown crash, look for low-risk investment bargains among closed-end funds.

In a liquidation panic - such as during the 2008-09 financial crisis, or the COVID-19 stock-market crisis of March 2020 - these funds often fall to huge discounts to their underlying net asset value, offering what may be the closest thing you'll ever see to a free lunch.

To be sure, nobody knows if this turmoil will develop into a major crash or a bear market. So far, the selloff - although it seems steep now - should be viewed in context. It's barely six weeks since the S&P 500 was at all-time highs. Since then, it's down only about 8%. The index is still up about 5% this year.

What will happen next? Screenwriter William Goldman's famous comment about Hollywood applies equally well to Wall Street. "Nobody knows anything. Not one person in the entire motion picture field knows for a certainty what's going to work."

But it's a matter of being prepared. Those who bought stocks during past panics generally earned spectacular investment returns - so long as they bought wisely, of course.

Closed-end funds are the redheaded stepchild of the mutual-fund industry. Unlike exchange-traded funds and traditional mutual funds, they don't issue new shares when investors put money into the fund, and they don't redeem the shares when investors sell. Instead, there are a limited number of shares, and they trade on the market like a company's shares. To invest in the fund, an investor would need to get their broker to buy them off an existing investor who wants to sell. For those wanting to get out of the fund, they would need to find an investor who wants to buy.

This unique feature gives closed-end funds one special characteristic: The share price is not governed by the underlying net asset value of the fund's investments. A closed-end fund could theoretically own, say, $10 a share in no-risk Treasury bills, but the share price could still fly all over the place based on what's happening in the stock market.

In a crash, the share prices often fall off a cliff. Far more so than the underlying investments. So this can give investors a double bargain: The stocks, bonds and so on that the fund holds may have gone down with the market, making them cheaper, while the stock of the fund itself may have fallen even further.

At the depths of the March 2020 COVID panic, solid, well-run closed-end funds that invested in everything from stocks to real estate to municipal bonds saw their fund's shares fall to 20% or more below the underlying value of the investments - which were, themselves, sharply down. When the market recovered, the investments rose - and the share price rose even more.

There are hundreds of funds out there, and they range from the excellent to the dismal.

One worth a look (for example) is Source Capital SOR.

This is a conservative "balanced portfolio" fund run by FPA Advisors, a firm known for its cautious approach to markets. It successfully dodged the infamous dot-com bubble at the turn of the millennium and suffered comparatively small losses during the global financial crisis of 2008-09. Over the past 10 years, Source has outperformed its benchmark, which is a theoretical portfolio consisting of 60% global equities and 40% U.S. bonds. The fund is co-managed by Steve Romick, better known for running the $12.5 billion FPA Crescent FPACX mutual fund. (Source has just $410 million in assets.)

Source came into this selloff conservatively positioned. That included a hefty 16% of the portfolio held in cash and equivalents, such as Treasury bills. FPA partner Ryan Leggio told me the cash position is unusually high because the fund has been selling bonds this year and hasn't found enough good value investment opportunities.

He said the fund has a policy of buying back shares in the market whenever the discount to net asset value is more than 10%. After the turmoil of recent weeks, SOR at $45.50 a share on Thursday was selling at a 9% discount, equivalent to buying investments at 91 cents on the dollar.

The fees, 0.98% a year, are higher than in most low-cost index funds. But then there's the discount, the outperformance, and all that cash on the balance sheet.

None of this means a full-blown crash will happen. But it's always good to be prepared.

-Brett Arends

data.title: Canada Retail Sales Pull Back After 0.8% Rise in September — Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadian shoppers look to have reined in their spending in October after higher prices at the pump drove an increase in retail sales in the month before.

The value of retail trade in the country increased 0.8% in September from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 75.31 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.51 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday. That was a tick stronger than the 0.7% advance economists expected and followed upwardly revised growth of 1.4% in August.

An early look at receipts indicates sales in October dropped 1.5%, which would be the sharpest fall since February 2025.

That estimate suggests a soft start to the final quarter of 2026. Households have so far weathered heightened trade and economic uncertainty and the shock of elevated energy costs, but the job market has struggled in recent months and the central bank in late October raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years.

Statistics Canada offered no detail with its October estimate, which was based on the responses of roughly 58% of retailers surveyed and will be revised.

The data agency's survey for showed sales in September were up in five of the nine industry segments it tracks, led by trade at gasoline stations and fuel vendors. Stripping out fuel, sales edged up 0.1 for the month.

In volume terms, sales overall were up a modest 0.1% in September and 3.4% above the level a year earlier.

Total sales for the third quarter increased 1.2%, softening from the prior quarter's 2.2% growth, though the volume of trade for the latest quarter was up 1% versus a softer 0.4% in the second quarter.

Consumer spending has remained solid this year, and is expected by the Bank of Canada to help underpin a recovery in economic growth in 2027. Still, there are concerns households will cut back on outlays the longer energy costs remain elevated.

The Bank of Canada's focus on rising inflation risk prompted it to raise its policy interest rate. Annual inflation has been at, or above, the upper end of the bank's 1%-3% control range four months running, holding at 3.1% in October even as underlying measures of core inflation have remained more contained.

The September retail data showed gas and fuel sales were up a second month in a row, increasing 6.9% in nominal terms and 1.6% on a volume basis.

Sales at motor vehicle and parts dealers also rose a second consecutive month, climbing 0.2% from the prior month thanks to growth at new core dealers.

Core sales, which strips out both fuel and autos, nudged up 0.1% for the month with a boost from general merchandise stores. Canadians also spent more on clothing, accessories, luggage and leather goods and on health and personal care in September.

The sharpest fall came from food and beverage sales, driven by weakness at supermarkets and other grocery retailers.

The Bank of Canada projects the economy will slow in the final quarter of 2026 as the country adjusts to the latest U.S. tariffs, then recover next year. An estimate of industry accounts suggests gross domestic product contracted 0.1% between August and September after essentially no change the previous two months.

At the same time, employment in Canada has fallen three months running, driving the jobless rate in October to a six-month high of 6.7%.

data.title: Oconee Federal to Merge With Pee Dee Federal Savings Bank
data.description:
Oconee Federal to Merge With Pee Dee Federal Savings Bank

Oconee Federal Financial Corp. (OTCQX: OFED) (the “Company”), the holding company for Oconee Federal Savings and Loan Association (“Oconee Federal”), and the majority-owned subsidiary of Oconee Federal, MHC (the “MHC”), and Pee Dee Federal Savings Bank (“Pee Dee”), a federally-chartered mutual savings bank, today announced the execution of an agreement pursuant to which Pee Dee will merge with and into Oconee Federal with Oconee Federal as the surviving entity. The merger is expected to increase the Company’s consolidated assets from $668 million at September 30, 2026 to $699 million based on Pee Dee’s assets as of September 30, 2026.

Pee Dee’s office will become a branch office of Oconee Federal. Under terms of the agreement, depositors of Pee Dee will become depositors of Oconee Federal and members of the MHC, and will have the same rights and privileges in the MHC as if their accounts had been established in Oconee Federal on the date established at Pee Dee. As part of the transaction, the Company will issue shares of its common stock to the MHC in an amount equal to the fair value of Pee Dee as determined by a third-party appraisal. These shares are expected to be issued concurrently with the completion of the merger. In addition, Oconee Federal plans to establish a Marion Advisory Board consisting of the non-employee directors of Pee Dee.

The proposed merger is expected to be immediately accretive to the Company’s earnings in 2027 and thereafter, and immediately accretive to its tangible book value per share. Upon completion of the merger, Oconee Federal’s capital ratios are expected to continue to exceed “well capitalized” regulatory standards.

Curtis Evatt, Chief Executive Officer of Oconee Federal, stated, “We are very pleased to announce our partnership with Pee Dee Federal Savings Bank. We look forward to welcoming Pee Dee’s customers and continuing to support the communities Pee Dee has served for over 90 years.”

George McMillan II, President and Chief Executive Officer of Pee Dee, said, “Oconee Federal’s larger size will enable us to enhance the products and services we offer our customers, while its long-established community bank culture will allow us to continue to provide personalized service and support for the Marion community.”

The transaction is expected to close in the second quarter of 2027. The transaction is subject to certain conditions, including the approval by Pee Dee’s depositors and customary regulatory approvals.

Oconee Federal has six branch offices located in Oconee, Pickens and Darlington counties, South Carolina and two in Stephens and Clayton counties, Georgia.

Capital Resources Group, Inc. served as financial advisor to Oconee Federal and Olsen Palmer LLC served as financial advisor to Pee Dee. Luse Gorman, PC acted as legal counsel to Oconee Federal and Bradley Arant Boult Cummings LLP acted as legal counsel to Pee Dee.

data.title: 75% of Brand Leaders Worry AI Assistants Could Steer Shoppers to Competitors, Recom Study Finds
data.description:
75% of Brand Leaders Worry AI Assistants Could Steer Shoppers to Competitors, Recom Study Finds

  • Most brands see AI transforming product discovery, but few feel ready to compete
  • Brands with a dedicated, resourced AI shopping effort are five times as likely to be very confident of hitting 2026 marketplace targets

Brand leaders overwhelmingly expect AI to change how shoppers find products, but few say they are ready, according to new research from Recom, the commerce operating partner that helps ambitious brands grow everywhere people shop.

In a recent Recom survey of 150+ brand leaders, 78% of respondents expect AI to influence the majority of product discovery in their category within three years. Only 12% say their brand is “very prepared” to reach shoppers who research products in plain language.

The findings, published today in Recom’s AI Commerce Readiness Gap Report, show a widening divide between brands investing in AI-driven shopping and those waiting on the sidelines.

“If you look at the brands that dominated Amazon over the last two decades, a lot of them didn’t have the best products, they just got there first,” said Recom Chief Growth Officer Sam Gagliardi. “AI shopping is having that same moment. Our research shows brands see it coming but haven’t really started positioning themselves to own the next decade of shopping. The brands putting real resources behind AI shopping already feel more confident about their growth, and we see that with our brand partners every day.”

Brands investing in AI shopping are pulling ahead

Leaders broadly agree the way shoppers discover products is changing, yet 81% say their teams lack skills their company needs to compete in AI-driven commerce. Almost one in four (23%) have no clear owner for AI shopping readiness or don’t know who it is.

The gap carries real competitive risk. Three in four leaders (75%) worry AI assistants could steer shoppers to competitors’ products. Leaders whose brands have a dedicated, resourced AI shopping effort are five times as likely as those taking no action to be very confident of hitting their 2026 marketplace targets. They’re also almost twice as likely to feel prepared for plain-language shopping.

Today, 46% of brands have made AI shopping a resourced priority, 31% are exploring it without committed resources, and 22% haven’t acted.

Marketplace fundamentals still matter most

However shopping behavior changes, leaders see marketplace fundamentals as the biggest growth levers they can pull. Asked which single fix would add the most revenue in the next 12 months, 33% chose product listing quality and content, followed by inventory availability and fulfillment speed (22%) and pricing control and consistency (19%). Seventy percent agree marketplace fundamentals will matter more as AI shopping grows.

A cautious outlook for the rest of 2026

The readiness gap may help explain why leaders are measured about the months ahead. Only half (50%) expect a better holiday season than 2025, even as 77% feel confident they will hit their 2026 revenue targets. Tariffs and import costs top leaders’ concerns (54%), ahead of softening consumer demand (41%) and rising advertising costs (40%).

What brands can do now

The report recommends three steps for brands: make their catalogs legible to AI, measure what AI says about their brand, and resource AI shopping like any other channel, with an owner, a budget, and a target.

The full The AI Commerce Readiness Gap Report, including tips on what brands can do now, is available at recom.com/news-ideas/the-ai-commerce-readiness-gap.

About Recom

Founded in 2013, Recom helps leading consumer brands — including JBL, Philips Hue, Brooks Running, and Sisley Paris — grow across marketplaces, social commerce, and emerging AI-driven channels. Recom unifies retail operations, advertising, content, pricing, logistics, fulfillment, and data science into one integrated system, giving brands a single engine for marketplace growth. The company has surpassed $700 million in annual revenue by building the frontier systems consumer brands need to win in an AI-powered economy, reaching consumers wherever and however they prefer to discover and buy. To learn more, visit recom.com.

data.title: enVVeno Medical Presents Three-Year Surgical Venous Valve Replacement Data Showing Sustained Clinical Benefit and Highlights Next-Generation enVVe Transcatheter System at the 53rd Annual VEITH Symposium
data.description:
IRVINE, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / enVVeno Medical Corporation (Nasdaq:NVNO) ("enVVeno Medical" or the "Company"), a company setting new standards of care for the treatment of deep venous disease, will present three-year data from SAVVE, the U.S. pivotal study of the VenoValve® today at the 53rd Annual Vascular and Endovascular Issues, Techniques and Horizons (VEITH) Symposium in New York City. The data, which will be presented by Dr. David Dexter of Sentara Vascular Specialists, shows sustained, statistically significant improvements in the revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), leg pain and quality-of-life measures in patients with severe chronic venous insufficiency (CVI). The presentation will also highlight enVVe®, the Company's next-generation, non-surgical transcatheter replacement venous valve.

Among the data being presented at VEITH are:

  • 5.8-point average improvement in disease severity, as measured by rVCSS, from baseline to 36 months.
  • 18-point and 19-point average improvements in venous disease-specific quality of life (VEINES-QOL) and symptoms (VEINES-Sym), respectively.

The rVCSS is a clinically validated scoring system used to track the progression or regression of venous diseases, and a 5.8-point improvement represents a real difference in the daily lives of these patients. Improvement was observed as early as three months following implantation and was sustained through 36 months.

"Patients improved significantly after receiving the VenoValve, and this three-year data shows that those benefits have been sustained," said Robert Berman, Chief Executive Officer of enVVeno Medical. "Demonstrating the long-term viability of our replacement venous valve technology is critically important as we advance enVVe."

enVVe, the Company's next-generation, non-surgical replacement venous valve, builds on the clinical experience gained with VenoValve. Unlike VenoValve, which requires an open surgical procedure and an overnight hospital stay, enVVe is designed to be implanted in a less invasive procedure performed under light sedation, with patients expected to go home the same day.

enVVe will be evaluated in TAVVE (TrAnscatheter Venous Valve Endoprosthesis), a prospective, multicenter pivotal study that received FDA Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) authorization in April 2026. Part 1 of the TAVVE pivotal study will consist of up to 10 patients who will initially be monitored for safety. Following FDA review, the Company plans to proceed to Part 2 of the TAVVE pivotal study, which will evaluate regurgitant flow volume and rVCSS, along with other secondary endpoints. The Company remains on track to enroll the first patient in TAVVE by year-end 2026.

About the enVVe System

The investigational enVVe System is a transcatheter-delivered replacement venous valve designed to restore one-way blood flow in the deep veins of patients with chronic venous insufficiency. An estimated 3 million people in the U.S. suffer from severe deep venous insufficiency, and it remains one of the largest unmet needs in vascular medicine. As venous valves fail, patients often experience chronic pain, swelling, skin changes, recurrent venous leg ulcers and declining quality of life.

Despite the significant burden of deep venous insufficiency, treatment options remain limited and are primarily focused on managing symptoms through compression therapy and wound care rather than addressing the underlying cause: dysfunctional venous valves. The enVVe System is being developed to address this critical treatment gap by helping restore proper directional blood flow to the deep venous system.

About the SAVVE Study

The SAVVE (Surgical Anti-reflux Venous Valve Endoprosthesis) study is a prospective, single-arm, multicenter U.S. pivotal clinical study evaluating VenoValve in 75 patients with severe chronic venous insufficiency due to deep venous reflux across 21 U.S. clinical centers. The study includes patients with CEAP clinical classifications C4b through C6 and evaluates changes in disease severity, pain, quality of life, symptoms, venous ulcer area and device patency, with follow-up extending to five years.

About enVVeno Medical Corporation

enVVeno Medical (NASDAQ:NVNO) is an Irvine, California-based, late clinical-stage medical device company focused on the advancement of innovative bioprosthetic (tissue-based) solutions to improve the standard of care for the treatment of deep venous disease.

data.title: Kelt Forge Launches AI-Powered Platform That Puts Custom Software Development Within Reach of Everyone
data.description:
Kelt Forge Launches AI-Powered Platform That Puts Custom Software Development Within Reach of Everyone

Kelt Forge Launches AI-Powered Platform That Puts Custom Software Development Within Reach of Everyone

PR Newswire

MISSION VIEJO, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026

Starting at just $25 per month, Kelt Forge helps entrepreneurs and small businesses turn ideas into websites, web apps and mobile applications without traditional programming.

MISSION VIEJO, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kelt Agentic Systems, LLC today announced the launch of Kelt Forge, an AI-powered software creation platform designed to help individuals and businesses build the technology they imagine. Starting at just $25 per month, the platform offers a new way to create, refine and expand software using everyday language.

Instead of starting with a development team or learning to code, users describe what they want to build. Kelt Forge helps generate the software, provides tools to make changes, and offers interactive previews so users can see their ideas take shape. The platform supports business websites, web applications, and iOS and Android mobile projects.

Turning Imagination Into Reality

For small businesses, the challenge is often not a lack of ideas but the cost and complexity of bringing them to life. A company might need a customer portal, a quoting system, an internal operations dashboard or a mobile experience tailored to how its team actually works. Off-the-shelf software may require businesses to change their processes; traditional custom development can put more ambitious ideas out of reach.

Kelt Forge is built around a different approach: describe a need, create a working starting point and continue improving it as the business evolves. Users can return to a project, request new features, review changes and move toward publishing from the same workspace. The goal is to make software creation an ongoing capability.

Founder Ken Eynon drew on his experience building and improving software for Sivility Systems, including websites, accounting-related workflows and sales tools. That experience shaped his belief that business owners should be able to create technology around their operations instead of forcing their operations to fit someone else's software.

"For $25 a month, you're not just investing in software. You're investing in the freedom to keep creating," said Eynon.

Kelt Forge combines AI-assisted development, project iteration and platform-specific preview and publishing workflows in one environment. Mobile app distribution remains subject to the applicable Apple and Google developer-account requirements and approvals.

Kelt Forge is designed for entrepreneurs, small-business owners and creators who want to turn practical ideas into useful digital products, from stronger online experiences to custom operational tools.

Learn more at www.kelt.com.

About Kelt Agentic Systems, LLC

Based in Mission Viejo, California, Kelt Agentic Systems, LLC develops Kelt Forge, an AI-powered platform that helps people create websites, web applications and mobile software. Its mission is to make custom software creation more accessible and adaptable for businesses and individuals.

data.title: Biotricity Reports Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results
data.description:
Revenue up 11.5%, gross margin 83.3% and income from operations up 23.7%. 

REDWOOD CITY, CA , Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Biotricity Inc. (OTCQB: BTCY) ("Biotricity" or the "Company"), a medical technology company providing remote cardiac monitoring solutions, announced its financial results for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, ended September 30, 2026.

Dr. Waqaas Al-Siddiq, Biotricity Founder and CEO, said, "Our second quarter delivered year-over-year growth in technology fee revenue, a higher gross margin and operating leverage. Revenue grew 11.5%, gross margin expanded to 83.3% and income from operations rose 23.7%, as gross profit growth outpaced higher operating expenses, including the timing of research and development activities."

Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Highlights (compared to the second quarter of fiscal 2026)

  • Revenue increased 11.5% to $4.33 million. Technology fee revenue, the majority of which is recurring, increased 13.3% to $3.98 million, or 91.8% of total revenue (prior-year quarter: 90.4%).
  • Gross margin improved to 83.3% from 81.9%, driven by technology fee gross margin of 85.5% (prior-year quarter: 82.3%). Gross profit increased 13.4% to $3.61 million.
  • Operating expenses increased 12.5% to $3.27 million, primarily due to a 46.7% increase in research and development expenses to $0.88 million; selling, general and administrative expenses increased 3.5% from increased sales. Income from operations increased 23.7% to $339 thousand, an operating margin of 7.8% (prior-year quarter: 7.0%).
  • Net loss before dividends was $0.81 million (prior-year quarter: $0.69 million), including a $151 thousand non-cash loss on the change in fair value of derivative liabilities. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $0.95 million, or $(0.046) per share, compared to $0.77 million, or $(0.029) per share, on fewer weighted average shares.

Six-Month Highlights (compared to the prior-year period)

  • Revenue increased 11.0% to $8.61 million, driven by an 18.3% increase in technology fee revenue. Gross margin improved to 82.9% from 81.2%.
  • Net loss before dividends was $1.77 million (prior-year period: $1.36 million). Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $2.02 million, or $(0.092) per share, compared to $1.53 million, or $(0.057) per share.
  • Net cash provided by operating activities was $511 thousand (prior-year period: $42 thousand), primarily reflecting higher accounts payable, accrued liabilities and collections of accounts receivable.

Corporate Developments

  • The Company signed a national distribution agreement, subject to a successful pilot program, where the partner will fund commercial expansion in exchange for a 30% distribution margin. The 18-month pilot was officially kicked off in October and is restricted to 6 states. Upon a successful pilot, the program will be expanded.
  • In October 2026, the Company was selected to provide cardiac screenings to patients in low-income communities and developing countries under a charitably funded program. The Company will be paid in advance at its standard commercial rates and currently expects the program to involve the deployment of at least 1,000 devices; there can be no assurance as to the timing or extent of deployment or the revenue ultimately recognized.
  • Successfully established a long-term inventory financing program to fund production.

Full results are included in the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, filed on November 16, 2026 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and available at www.sec.gov.

About Biotricity Inc.

Biotricity is reforming the healthcare market by bridging the gap in remote monitoring and chronic cardiac care. Doctors and patients trust Biotricity's unparalleled standard for preventive & personal care, including diagnostic and post-diagnostic solutions for cardiac conditions. The Company develops comprehensive remote health monitoring solutions for the medical and consumer markets. To learn more, visit www.biotricity.com.

data.title: JAMA Study Using Alamar Biosciences’ NULISA Assay Links Blood eMTBR-tau to Tau tangle Burden in Former Football Players with Advanced CTE
data.description:
FREMONT, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Alamar Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALMR), a leader in precision proteomics dedicated to enabling the earliest detection of disease, today announced new research published in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA). Researchers at Boston University CTE Center, with collaborators at Banner Health and more than 20 Institutions, used Alamar’s NULISAqpcr™ eMTBR-tau single-plex assay to evaluate whether a blood test could identify chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) pathology in living patients.

The researchers found higher blood levels of eMTBR-tau in former football players with advanced CTE and that levels rose with the amount of tau tangle pathology in the brain. eMTBR-tau is a protein fragment linked to the tau tangles seen in CTE and Alzheimer’s disease. CTE is a. neurodegenerative disease associated with repeated head impacts. Today it can only be confirmed by examining the brain after death. The finding could give researchers a way to study CTE during life.

“CTE has been extraordinarily difficult to study because doctors cannot confirm it in a living person. Proteins like eMTBR-tau have recently been associated with neuropathology but are present at very low levels in blood,” said Yuling Luo, PhD, founder, CEO and chair of Alamar Biosciences. “Our NULISA technology was built to measure low abundant proteins, and a reliable, simple blood test for CTE would enable new research into the progression and treatment of this debilitating illness. There is more work to do, but studies like this one show why that effort matters.”

The study included 21 former American football players who gave blood samples during life and later donated their brains for research through Boston University CTE Center Studies. Eighteen had CTE, including 16 with high-stage disease. Plasma eMTBR-tau was significantly higher in high-stage CTE than in low-stage CTE or no CTE. Five of the CTE cases also had Alzheimer’s disease, and eMTBR-tau levels were highest in people who had both conditions. The researchers also measured p-tau217, an established blood marker for Alzheimer’s disease. It was elevated only in people with Alzheimer’s pathology and was not associated with CTE. Used together, the two markers may help researchers tell the conditions apart.

The study suggests a promising new biomarker approach to accurately detecting CTE pathology through a blood test, with the potential to improve patient diagnosis, identification and enrollment in clinical trials, and support the development of targeted therapies. The researchers describe the results as an early study that requires validation in larger and diverse cohorts. The test is not a diagnostic tool and is not available for clinical use. To date, no blood test has yet been validated for diagnosing CTE in living patients.

“Having blood tests that accurately determine the underlying pathology, which are now approved for use in Alzheimer’s disease, has been revolutionary in the way we diagnose patients and design therapeutic trials,” said Nicholas Ashton, PhD, co-senior author of the study and senior director of Banner Health’s Fluid Biomarker Program. “With this new study, we are optimistic this biomarker will spur a serious discussion about treatment development for CTE.”

Dr. Ashton’s work also includes blood-based eMTBR-tau measurement in Alzheimer’s disease, most recently in a JAMA study published November 16 that used a NULISA-based assay to assess tau pathology in plasma from 728 research participants.

About Alamar Biosciences

Alamar is a commercial-stage proteomics company establishing a gold standard in protein detection and analysis. Leveraging our proprietary NULISA™ technology and the ARGO® HT System, our platform is designed to detect protein biomarkers at extremely low concentrations in blood with ultra-high sensitivity, high specificity, flexible multiplexing, broad dynamic range and seamless automation. We refer to this combination of features as “Precision Proteomics,” and believe it fills a critical gap in the field of advanced proteomics, helping researchers unlock the full spectrum of protein biomarkers across disease states. Learn more at alamarbio.com.

data.title: Polaryx Therapeutics Highlights Participation in NCL Scientific Conference and NTSAD Imagine & Believe Event
data.description:
PARAMUS, NJ, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Polaryx Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: PLYX) ("Polaryx" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel, disease-modifying therapies for rare pediatric lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs), today highlighted its participation in the 9th NCL Translational Science and Therapeutics Conference and the National Tay-Sachs & Allied Diseases Association’s (NTSAD) Imagine & Believe event in the Boston area. The Company’s participation reflects its commitment to engaging with researchers, clinicians, patient advocates and families as it advances development of its lead investigational drug candidate, PLX-200, across four rare pediatric LSDs.

At the NCL conference, held November 11–13, 2026, at the Marriott Boston Quincy in Quincy, Massachusetts, Will Charlton, M.D., M.A.S., Polaryx Therapeutics’ Chief Medical Officer, presented an update on the Company’s development program, including previously published preclinical findings in a CLN3 mouse model. His presentation took place on Friday, November 13, as part of the session titled, “Clinical Program Updates II: Small Molecules, ERTs and Other Therapeutic Approaches.”

Polaryx was also represented by Shrijay Vijayan, Ph.D. MBA, Chief Scientific Officer, and Minsu Kang, Ph.D., Vice President of Clinical Development and Regulatory Affairs and the conference brought together scientists, clinicians, industry representatives and patient advocacy organizations focused on advancing research and therapeutic development for neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses (NCLs), commonly known as Batten disease. CLN2 and CLN3 disease are among the four indications being evaluated in Polaryx’s SOTERIA Phase 2 basket trial of orally administered PLX-200.

“Advancing therapies for rare pediatric diseases requires close engagement with the scientific community and the families whose lives are affected by these conditions,” said Alex Yang, Polaryx Therapeutics’ Chair and Chief Executive Officer. “Following activation of our first SOTERIA clinical trial site, these events provided an important opportunity to share our development progress and reinforce our commitment to the patient communities we aim to serve. We remain focused on translating our research into carefully conducted clinical studies that can help address the significant unmet needs of children and families living with these devastating diseases.”

Members of the Polaryx team also attended NTSAD’s Imagine & Believe dinner on November 12, 2026, at the Hyatt Regency Boston/Cambridge. Polaryx supported the event as a sponsor. The annual fundraiser brings together families, researchers, industry representatives and advocates to support research, family services and advocacy for Tay-Sachs, Canavan, GM1 and Sandhoff diseases. Sandhoff disease is also one of the four indications included in SOTERIA.

Polaryx recently announced activation of the first SOTERIA clinical trial site at Boys Town National Research Hospital in Nebraska. SOTERIA is designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and clinical activity of PLX-200 in children with CLN2 disease, CLN3 disease, Krabbe disease and Sandhoff disease.

About the SOTERIA Trial

SOTERIA is a Phase 2, open-label, single arm trial intended to assess the safety, tolerability, and clinical activity of Polaryx’s lead drug candidate, PLX-200, in CLN2, CLN3, Krabbe disease, and Sandhoff disease, four different LSDs whose patient populations Polaryx believes represent approximately one quarter of the LSD population. SOTERIA is designed to be flexible, resource-efficient, and provide important data and information important to PLX-200’s future clinical development.  Polaryx received a safe to proceed letter in October 2025 from the FDA and plans to initiate SOTERIA in the fourth quarter of 2026 in trial sites in the United States as well as in Europe and Asia or other foreign jurisdictions. Designed with a high degree of flexibility, SOTERIA represents a resource-efficient opportunity to validate PLX-200’s preclinical science across multiple LSDs while gathering data to inform planning PLX-200’s future development pathway, including the initiation of potentially pivotal trials. For the CLN2 and CLN3 cohorts, although the entire trial is open label, these cohorts will incorporate analyses comparing natural history data as a control arm to PLX-200’s treated arm. A natural history study is a preplanned observational study intended to track the course of the disease. Should the data demonstrate compelling clinical activity, Polaryx may pursue an expedited approval pathway. For more information about the SOTERIA trial, please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07740512.

About Polaryx Therapeutics

Polaryx Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing patient-friendly small molecule and gene therapy treatments for rare orphan lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs). Founded in 2014, Polaryx seeks to deliver safe, effective, and patient-friendly treatments that address the underlying pathophysiology of these catastrophic diseases and their significant unmet need. Our approach integrates small molecule therapies, including a combination therapy, and a gene therapy, positioning us to potentially address both the genetic and downstream pathological features of LSDs. Our small molecule drug candidates share similar modes of action that have been demonstrated to address lysosomal dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and neuronal loss in our validated animal models that closely mimic human clinical phenotypes. Our most advanced product candidate, PLX-200, targets several LSDs and we intend to launch SOTERIA, a Phase 2 basket trial, to evaluate PLX-200’s safety and efficacy in the fourth quarter of 2026. For more information about the SOTERIA trial, please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07740512. More information about Polaryx may be found at www.polaryx.com.
